title: Mood-Shape
primitive: the felt-shape a tale leaves in the room (the mood after the last word)
summary: Every told tale leaves a feeling in the room — funny, scary, tender, wild. This kit listens for what mood actually lands when the tale ends, and whether the teller meant for it to land that way. Phase 2 deepens the Phase 1 mood-tag with a kid-readable model: mood is the SHAPE of what you left behind, not the sticker you put on it.

questions.prompt: Tell a 60-second tale. Don't pick a mood first. After you finish, sit for one breath — then name the mood the room is sitting in. Did the mood you wanted match the mood that arrived?
When the mood at the END of your tale is different from the mood you were aiming for, what's usually the strongest move?
options: Re-tell with a different opening line.
Keep the tale, change the mood tag — let the listener vote with their feet.
Slow the Close beat and add one small detail that pulls toward the mood you wanted.
questions.rationale: Mood lives in the Close. A single specific Close-beat detail (a smell, a sound, a small movement) can rotate the felt-shape without changing the whole tale. Changing the opening rebuilds the room from scratch; changing the tag is honest but lets the tale stay misshapen.

questions.prompt: Pick a tale from your anthology with a strong mood. What was the smallest moment that decided the mood — a word, a pause, the tone of one line? Could that moment be moved?

Take a funny tale you've told and rewrite the Close beat to land tender instead. Keep every event the same. Change only the tone of the last two lines — see how small a move it takes to shift the room.

castCameos.line: I lean in when the mood matches what the teller's body is doing — when the breath and the words agree, the room agrees.
Mood pivots in the last beat. The whole tale is preparing the listener to FEEL a thing — make the felt-thing arrive on purpose.
A long pause at the Close is a mood-tool. The room will fill the silence with the mood you set up.
If the same image returns at the Hook and the Close, the mood is doubled — listeners FEEL the bookend before they notice it.
